soccer.definition: A football game in which two teams of 11 players try to kick or head a ball into the opponents' goal.

basketball.definition: A game played on a court by two opposing teams of 5 players.

tennis.definition: A game played with rackets by two or four players who hit a ball back and forth over a net that divides the court.

volleyball.definition: A game in which two teams hit an inflated ball over a high net using their hands.

baseball.definition: A ball game played with a bat and ball between two teams of nine players.

football.definition: A team sport, called American football, using an oval ball carried or passed toward an end zone.

rugby.definition: A form of football played with an oval ball.

cricket.definition: A game played with a ball and bat by two teams of 11 players.

badminton.definition: A game played by hitting a shuttlecock over a net.

table-tennis.definition: A racket game similar to tennis, it is played across a table with paddles and a lightweight hollow ball.

golf.definition: A sport in which players hit a small ball into a series of holes.

bowling.definition: A sport in which players roll a heavy ball to knock down pins.

ball.definition: A round or oval object used for throwing, kicking or striking in games.

racket.definition: A sports tool with a handle and framed striking surface, often strung, used to hit a ball or shuttlecock.

bat.definition: A club-like sports tool used to strike a ball; its material and shape depend on the game.

helmet.definition: A hard covering worn to protect the head.

shin-guard.definition: A protective pad worn over the front of the lower leg during some sports.
shin-guard.exampleUsage: The football player wore a shin guard under each sock.

knee-pad.definition: A protective pad worn over one knee.

glove.definition: A covering worn on a hand for grip or protection; designs differ by sport.

net.definition: A mesh structure used across a court or as part of a goal or hoop.

goal.definition: A frame or net where players score points.

hoop.definition: Here, the circular ring used as a basketball scoring target.

scoreboard.definition: A large board for displaying the score of a contest (and some other information).

whistle.definition: A small object blown to make a loud signal.

stopwatch.definition: A watch that measures how long an activity takes.

cone.definition: A cone-shaped marker used to mark a sports area or practice route.

running.definition: Moving quickly on foot during play or exercise.

sprinting.definition: Running as fast as possible over a short distance.

relay-race.definition: A team race in which participants complete successive stages, often passing a baton.

hurdles.definition: A footrace in which contestants must negotiate a series of hurdles.

long-jump.definition: A sport in which an athlete runs and jumps as far as possible.

high-jump.definition: An athletics event in which competitors jump over a raised horizontal bar.

javelin.definition: An athletic competition in which a javelin is thrown as far as possible.

discus.definition: An athletic competition in which a disk-shaped object is thrown as far as possible.

pole-vault.definition: A track-and-field event in which competitors use a flexible pole to clear a high crossbar.

marathon.definition: A long-distance running race covering 42.195 kilometers.

starting-block.definition: A support athletes push against with their feet at the start of a sprint.

finish-line.definition: A line marking the point where a race ends.

swimming-pool.definition: A large basin filled with water where people swim, practice, relax, or compete.

diving-board.definition: A flexible platform that springs upward when a swimmer jumps from it to dive.

kickboard.definition: A floating board held during swimming practice to support the upper body while focusing on leg movement.
kickboard.exampleUsage: The swimmer used a kickboard during the supervised lesson.

swim-cap.definition: A close-fitting cap worn over the hair while swimming.
swim-cap.exampleUsage: She put on a swim cap before entering the pool.

backstroke.definition: A swimming stroke that resembles the crawl except the swimmer lies on his or her back.

freestyle.definition: A swimming event allowing a choice of stroke under its rules; in everyday usage it often means front crawl.

butterfly-stroke.definition: A swimming technique in which the swimmer faces downward, moves both arms over the water together, and uses a simultaneous dolphin kick.

water-polo.definition: A team sport in which swimmers compete in a pool, passing and throwing an inflated ball into the opposing team's goal.

synchronized-swimming.definition: A sport in which swimmers perform coordinated routines in the water, often to music; it is now commonly called artistic swimming.
synchronized-swimming.exampleUsage: The sports center hosts artistic-swimming practice.

gymnasium.definition: An indoor space equipped for exercise or sports.

locker-room.definition: A room in a sports facility or workplace where people change clothes and leave personal belongings in lockers.

bench.definition: A long seat that can accommodate more than one person.

bleachers.definition: Rows of tiered seats used by spectators at sports events.

track.definition: A prepared route or marked circuit used for running and athletics.

field.definition: An outdoor area used for playing sports.

court.definition: A marked area used for sports such as tennis, basketball, or volleyball.

ring.definition: A roped square area where boxing or wrestling takes place.

mat.definition: A thick flat pad used as a floor covering.

treadmill.definition: An exercise device consisting of an endless belt on which a person can walk or jog without changing place.
treadmill.exampleUsage: Dina asks staff where the treadmill is located.

weight-room.definition: A gym room containing equipment for strength and resistance training.
weight-room.exampleUsage: Staff explain the weight-room access rules to Dina.

shower.definition: A place or device that sprays water over you so you can wash your body.
shower.exampleUsage: Dina asks where the sports-center shower is located.

athlete.definition: A person trained to compete in sports.

coach.definition: A person who trains players in a sport.

referee.definition: (sports) the chief official (as in boxing or American football) who is expected to ensure fair play.

teammate.definition: A fellow member of a team.

warm-up.definition: To prepare for exercise with light or gradually increasing activity.
warm-up.exampleUsage: The coach asks the team to warm up before practice.

stretch.definition: To extend a body part or lengthen muscles during an appropriate movement.

score.definition: Here, to gain points or a goal in a game.

pass.definition: To send a ball to a teammate by the method allowed in a game.

kick.definition: To strike a ball or other object with a foot.

throw.definition: To send an object through the air with a movement of the hand and arm.

catch.definition: To receive and hold a moving object, often with the hands.

dribble.definition: To move with a ball by repeatedly bouncing it or controlling it with small touches.
